problem: Existing VLN benchmarks emphasize long-horizon room-to-room navigation with endpoint-only success, hiding failures in local, interaction-centric trajectory grounding (feasible approach, collision avoidance, action-compatible stopping) inside a single scene.
motivation: Embodied agents must approach objects from feasible directions, avoid clutter and stop at interaction-compatible locations. Current VLMs show weak embodied spatial grounding, but no benchmark tests continuous, executable trajectory prediction in a single 3D scene under interaction constraints.
key_idea: Build a scalable benchmark of text-to-3D single-scene environments with nine tiered (easy/medium/hard) instructions each, where VLMs predict coordinate waypoint trajectories scored pointwise by a GPT-5-mini judge on start, goal, obstacle avoidance and efficiency.
insight: Obstacle avoidance scores are high (0.84-0.91) while goal grounding is low (0.20-0.51), so the bottleneck is precise instruction-to-endpoint grounding rather than coarse geometry. Performance drops from easy to medium to hard (shown only in a figure), and qualitative failures are mislocalized starts, wrong goals and physically unsafe paths. Caveat: no judge validation (no human agreement) is provided, so the conclusions depend on an unvalidated GPT-5-mini judge.
method: Text-to-3D reconstruction: MS-COCO captions manually filtered/rewritten (1,200 stated in the method section; the FAQ says 1,000) and converted to single-scene 3D environments with Hunyuan3D-3.0, then manually filtered for coherence, navigability and geometry; final 2,472 environments.

Instruction generation: Qwen3-8B-VL sees top-down and oblique renders and produces 9 instructions per scene (3 each for easy navigation, medium 1-2 object interaction, hard 3+ object interaction), with banned viewpoint-relative words.
Trajectory prediction task: a frozen zero-shot VLM receives top-down + oblique views and the instruction and outputs integer waypoints on a 25x25x25 grid as JSON; deterministic decoding.

Pointwise judge protocol: GPT-5-mini scores each trajectory overlay 1-5 or N/A on start consistency, goal satisfaction, obstacle avoidance and efficiency; normalized to [0,1] and averaged per tier, then equal-weighted across tiers.
Humanoid visualization: GPT-5-mini waypoints animated with TLControl and MotionGPT as a qualitative executability check, not used for scoring.

setting.backbone: Qwen3-VL, Gemini Robotics ER-1.5, GPT-5-mini (frozen, zero-shot); judge GPT-5-mini
setting.observation: one rendered top-down view and one oblique view of a reconstructed single-scene 3D environment
setting.action_space: predicted sequence of integer 3D waypoints on a 25x25x25 grid (continuous trajectory)
setting.simulator: Hunyuan3D-3.0 generated static 3D scenes (no physics simulator)

numbers.extra: Judge-scored (GPT-5-mini) factor scores in [0,1], averaged over easy/medium/hard tiers; 2,472 scenes x 9 instructions

numbers_note: Per-tier results are only in a figure (no numbers). Paper text is mixed with unrelated LLM-adversarial content (ALKALI/GRACE), which was ignored. Evaluated models are benchmark baselines, not a proposed method; the 'SleepWalk' bench is the paper's own, and split labeled 'test' as a placeholder.
results: GPT-5-mini is best on all four factors (start 0.75, goal 0.51, obstacle 0.91, efficiency 0.64), beating Gemini Robotics ER-1.5 (0.58/0.34/0.89/0.58) and Qwen3-VL (0.48/0.20/0.84/0.47). All models fall from easy to hard tiers, and goal grounding is the weakest factor.
limitations: Evaluation relies on a single GPT-5-mini judge with no human-agreement, multi-judge or prompt-sensitivity validation; only three models and only top-down 2D overlay scoring.

Synthetic static generated scenes without physics; dataset construction is inconsistently documented (1,000/1,200 captions vs 2,472 scenes) and the paper text contains unrelated adversarial-LLM sections.
Coordinate-grid output format may confound spatial reasoning with interface difficulty; per-tier numbers are not tabulated.
